key_insight: Claim-level verification reduced hallucinated content by an order of magnitude, but verifier reliability—not answer generation—was the limiting factor.
clinical_relevance: Guideline-grounded AI answers still require oversight because verification can miss genuine errors and correction can introduce new ones.
method: Built 160 expert-approved questions across four ESC cardiology guidelines and 627 hand-verified retrieval records.
Tested a five-stage verification-and-correction pipeline under four retrieval configurations, with three runs each.
Manually audited 606 flagged claims, independently re-judged 906 decisions, and blindly reviewed 100 accepted claims.
evidence_signal: Across 1,920 arm-runs, only 44.7–50.6% of flagged claims were genuine hallucinations; single-run recall was 35.6–41.2%, and 1.7% of final answers contained genuine errors.
watch_item: Pipeline convergence did not guarantee correctness: 35% of genuine final errors were introduced during correction.
paper_title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Medical Question Answering on ESC Cardiology Guidelines: Evaluation and Retrieval Optimization
